html:
The Rankülche, or Ranqueles, are an Indigenous people of the dry plains of northern La Pampa and nearby provinces in Argentina. Their name means people of the reeds. They grew out of a mix of Puelche, Pehuenche and Tehuelche groups, and in the 1700s they took on the language and much of the culture of the Mapuche.

In the 18th and 19th centuries they were horse people who raised cattle and horses and traded and raided along the frontier with Buenos Aires and Córdoba. Their chiefs, such as Painé and Mariano Rosas, dealt with Argentine governments as equals. The writer Lucio V. Mansilla visited them in 1870 and wrote a famous account, Una excursión a los indios ranqueles.

In the Conquest of the Desert of 1878 to 1885 the Argentine army broke their independence and took their land. Neighbours: Huarpe and the Pampas peoples.
